dispositions.rationale: The challenge is correct on the pinned evidence: commit 54d60e9 contains no baseline-adoption reference in src/state/request-composition.ts, so the design as written documents no seam for drift recovery after the retirement deletes request-templates.ts. The wedge consequence does not hold for the phase's actual change set — the uncommitted working tree adds the composeGate arm and this session exercised it twice — but the design must say so: per the reviewer's own resolution (b), the surviving seam needs to be cited by file and line in the design and pinned by a test.
dispositions.revision_intent: Amend Section 1.3 amendment 1 so it names the surviving drift seam explicitly: the phase's change set composes kind "baseline-adoption" in composeGate (src/state/request-composition.ts, ahead of the phase approval gates, with the restore-applicability refusal recorded in archiveDirectSemanticGateDecision), and the semantic drift journey open → adopt-current-bytes / restore-recorded-bytes → resume is pinned by test/integration/status-reentry-edit.test.ts (including the baseline-adoption-restore-source-unavailable refusal). No code change: the bytes and the pinning test already exist in the phase's change set; the revision is the design citing them.
